tasks.task: Establish site, scaffold access, and occupant interface
tasks.scope: Mobilise plant, set up site compound via Kiora Lane and courtyard, establish occupant communication protocol, confirm scaffold access routes, prepare exclusion zones below work areas.
hazards: Trip and fall on site — uneven ground, debris, temporary works in compound and courtyard
Vehicle strike — plant and delivery movement on Kiora Lane and into courtyard with pedestrian and occupant traffic
Manual handling injury — moving plant, barriers, and compound equipment
Noise and dust disturbance to occupants — site activity during mobilisation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Vehicle strike — plant movement on shared access with occupant traffic
controls: Designate and barricade separate pedestrian route through courtyard — isolate from vehicle movement — before plant mobilisation starts.
Station traffic controller at Kiora Lane entry during all plant movements — direct vehicles and check for occupant pedestrians — continuous coverage.
Lay temporary safety matting on uneven ground in compound and courtyard — remove trip hazards before workers occupy site.
Establish one-way vehicle circulation in courtyard — marked with cones and directional signage — no reversing permitted.
Brief all occupants in writing on site activity schedule, noise hours, scaffold access routes, and contact number for site issues — deliver 48 hours before mobilisation.
Install perimeter hoarding below all scaffold levels — minimum 2.4 m high — exclusion zone under work marked on ground and signage posted.
Check all delivery vehicles and plant for defects, lights, reversing alarms, and spotter mirrors before entry — refuse entry if defective.
Assign dedicated plant operator for all on-site movement — no unauthorised machinery operation — operator to check clearance before each movement.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager

Scaffold component strike — tools or parts dropped during erection
Collapse or instability of partial scaffold — incomplete bracing or foundation failure during assembly
Electrical contact — scaffold near building services or live installations during positioning

Musculoskeletal injury — grinding, filling, and surface preparation by hand; repetitive motion and awkward postures

Apply wet suppression or dust extraction to all grinding work — no dry grinding of slab surface.
Maintain continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) at grinder discharge point during all surface preparation work.

tasks.scope: Demolish and remove tile bed, screed layer, and failed waterproofing membrane from all balcony surfaces. Manage silica dust control. Segregate and dispose of waste.
hazards: Inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust — removal of screed and tile bed by mechanical means
Exposure to asbestos fibres — if survey confirms asbestos in membrane or adhesives, disturbance during removal
Musculoskeletal injury — repetitive removal work, heavy lifting of waste, awkward postures on scaffold
Fall from height during waste removal — loss of balance or trip on uneven scaffold surface with debris

controls: Wet all surfaces with low-pressure water spray before starting mechanical removal. Maintain surface damp throughout work — do not allow dust to become airborne.
Use local dust extraction with HEPA filter connected to grinder or breaker during all cutting and breaking operations. Keep extraction nozzle within 300 mm of cut point.
Wear fitted P2 or P3 respirator — fit-tested and seal-checked before each shift. Minimum 2-hourly cartridge change or when breathing resistance increases.
Barricade balcony edge with exclusion netting or plywood boarding to prevent dust migration into occupied units below. Netting must be sealed at all gaps.
Remove and bag all tile, screed, and membrane debris immediately after breaking out. Store in sealed waste skip or bags on balcony — do not sweep or dry clean.
Monitor noise levels at operator position with sound meter before work start. If above 85 dB(A), provide double hearing protection (earplugs AND earmuffs) and record result.
Brief all workers on dust hazard, exclusion zone, and respiratory fit testing requirement before first shift. SDS for waterproofing membrane on point of use.
Stop all mechanical work if wet suppression system fails, water runoff enters occupied units, or dust escapes exclusion zone. tell supervisor immediately.

tasks.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to balcony slab
tasks.scope: Apply primer to prepared slab. Install new waterproofing membrane per manufacturer specification and engineer detail, including all penetrations, edges, and transitions. Cure per schedule before reinstatement.
hazards: Chemical inhalation or skin exposure — volatile organic compounds or solvents in primer, membrane, or adhesives
Fall from height — applicator movement on scaffold above 4m while carrying membrane rolls or application equipment
Inadequate curing — membrane not cured to specification before foot traffic or weather exposure, causing failure
Heat or UV sensitivity — rapid curing or weather interference affecting membrane bond or integrity
tasks.dominant_hazard: Chemical inhalation — application of primer and membrane with VOC or solvent content
controls: Obtain and read SDS for primer and membrane product at point of use before any application starts.
Confirm substrate is dry, clean, and free from dust, debris, or contamination — no application if wet or compromised.
Establish continuous forced ventilation across balcony using mechanical extraction or cross-breeze throughout application and cure phases.
Apply primer only when air temperature is 10–25°C and humidity below 85%; stop application if conditions exceed limits.
Install membrane in strict sequence per engineer detail and manufacturer specification — cover all penetrations, edges, and transitions without gaps or overlaps.
Prohibit foot traffic or equipment placement on uncured membrane — establish exclusion zone with barricade and signage.
Maintain cure schedule compliance — do not remove barriers or permit weather exposure until SDS cure time is confirmed elapsed.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection; change gloves immediately if contaminated.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: substrate condition is inspected and signed off by site supervisor and engineer confirms cure window conditions (temperature, humidity, weather forecast) are acceptable for next 48 hours minimum.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove exclusion barrier or allow foot traffic until: cure schedule time has elapsed and SDS cure specification is confirmed complete by applicator or supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails, wind gusts exceed 15 km/h, or VOC odour becomes strong — cease application until system is restored and air is clear.
🛑 STOP WORK if: temperature drops below 10°C, humidity exceeds 85%, or rain/dew is forecast within cure window — cover and cease work until conditions stabilise.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unexpected substrate condition (cracks, soft spots, contamination, or moisture) is found — obtain engineer approval before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tasks.task: Install screed layer and reinstate tiles to balcony surfaces
tasks.scope: Apply cement screed bed to cured membrane. Install tiles with appropriate adhesive and grout. Confirm level, slope, and drainage. Make good perimeter jointing.
hazards: Fall from height — installer and tiler movement on scaffold above 4m with tools and materials
Thermal or chemical exposure — screed mixing and cement contact causing skin irritation or chemical burn
Musculoskeletal injury — manual spreading of screed, tile placement, and grouting; repetitive bending and kneeling
Trip or slip on wet screed — newly applied screed before curing, creating slippery surface on scaffold
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — tiler and screed installer on scaffold above 4m
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate and competency tag fitted before any worker accesses scaffold.
Install edge protection (guardrails and toeboard) around all perimeter edges before screed or tiles start.
Wear full-body harness with lanyard clipped to fixed anchor point approved by engineer during all work above 4m.
Place wet screed warning signs on scaffold and adjacent ground areas. Establish no-go exclusion zone until screed cures (minimum 24 hours as per product SDS).
Review SDS for screed and tile adhesive on point of use. Confirm ventilation from occupied spaces below and weather window (no rain forecast, temperature 5–35°C) before starting.
Mix screed in small batches only. Wear chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection, and dust mask (P2) during mixing and application.
Apply screed using trowel or spreader. Do not kneel directly on freshly applied screed; use knee boards or crawling access only.
Set tiles to substrate with notched spreader. Check for void-free bed and level as per product requirements. Do not work on screed until surface has cured per SDS (typically 24 hours minimum).
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply screed until: scaffold handover certificate is signed, edge protection is complete, harness anchor points are approved by engineer, and weather window is confirmed (no rain, temperature 5–35°C, wind <20 km/h).

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install tiles or grout until: screed has cured for minimum 24 hours as confirmed by SDS and product instruction, and PM or licensed screed specialist has checked and signed substrate condition.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection becomes damaged, incomplete, or is removed; harness cannot be clipped to fixed anchor; or worker falls or is near-miss to edge.
🛑 STOP WORK if: rain begins, temperature falls below 5°C or exceeds 35°C, or wind speed exceeds 20 km/h (wind may displace debris netting and equipment).
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed base shows signs of movement, spalling, or unexpected softness; or if adhesive or grout SDS requirements cannot be met (ventilation, cure window, temperature).
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

hazards: Fall from height — erector contact with unprotected edges during scaffold installation above 4m
Scaffold component strike — tools or parts dropped during erection
Collapse or instability of partial scaffold — incomplete bracing or foundation failure during assembly
Electrical contact — scaffold near building services or live installations during positioning
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — erector working on incomplete scaffold above 4m
controls: Obtain and display signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any work starts.
Check scaffold design compliance with load calculations and working drawings before erection commences.
Establish exclusion zone at ground level — minimum 2m perimeter — barricade and sign to prevent public entry.
Install edge protection and guardrails to all open edges above 2m before any worker accesses incomplete scaffold.
Wear full body harness with shock absorber lanyard secured to dedicated anchor point during all erection work above 4m.
Use tool lanyards to prevent dropped tools; secure all small components in bags or tool belts during installation.
Brief all erectors on scaffold load capacity, anchor points, and no-go zones for incomplete bracing before work starts.
Verify electrical services isolated or capped before positioning scaffold within 1m of any live installation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow any worker on incomplete scaffold until: licenced scaffolder has issued written handover certificate confirming all bracing, guardrails, and edge protection installed and load capacity verified
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start erection above 4m until: certified scaffolder has approved foundation, base plate settlement, and levelness to within acceptable tolerance
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component is loose, bolt is missing, or bracing is incomplete during erection
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 40 km/h or weather becomes unsuitable for safe erection work
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by public, vehicles, or unauthorised personnel
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed, and tile bed
task_blocks_raw.scope: Demolish and remove tile bed, screed layer, and failed waterproofing membrane from all balcony surfaces. Manage silica dust control. Segregate and dispose of waste.
hazards: Inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust — removal of screed and tile bed by mechanical means
Exposure to asbestos fibres — if survey confirms asbestos in membrane or adhesives, disturbance during removal
Musculoskeletal injury — repetitive removal work, heavy lifting of waste, awkward postures on scaffold
Fall from height during waste removal — loss of balance or trip on uneven scaffold surface with debris
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of respirable crystalline silica dust — mechanical removal of screed and tile bed
controls: Wet all surfaces with low-pressure water spray before starting mechanical removal. Maintain surface damp throughout work — do not allow dust to become airborne.
Use local dust extraction with HEPA filter connected to grinder or breaker during all cutting and breaking operations. Keep extraction nozzle within 300 mm of cut point.
Wear fitted P2 or P3 respirator — fit-tested and seal-checked before each shift. Minimum 2-hourly cartridge change or when breathing resistance increases.
Barricade balcony edge with exclusion netting or plywood boarding to prevent dust migration into occupied units below. Netting must be sealed at all gaps.
Remove and bag all tile, screed, and membrane debris immediately after breaking out. Store in sealed waste skip or bags on balcony — do not sweep or dry clean.
Monitor noise levels at operator position with sound meter before work start. If above 85 dB(A), provide double hearing protection (earplugs AND earmuffs) and record result.
Brief all workers on dust hazard, exclusion zone, and respiratory fit testing requirement before first shift. SDS for waterproofing membrane on point of use.
Stop all mechanical work if wet suppression system fails, water runoff enters occupied units, or dust escapes exclusion zone. tell supervisor immediately.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start mechanical removal until: wet suppression and local dust extraction are tested and confirmed operational by supervisor
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next balcony section until: previous section debris is fully removed, bagged, and exclusion netting is re-sealed
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails, water pump is not functional, or surfaces dry faster than damp suppression can maintain
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extraction hose is damaged, blocked, or disconnected, or visible dust escapes exclusion zone

🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

task_blocks_raw.task: Investigate and document slab cracks and damage
task_blocks_raw.scope: check exposed slab for cracks, spalling, and structural damage. Photograph and map defects. Prepare defect schedule for engineer assessment.
hazards: Fall from height — work on balcony edge during inspection and photography above 4m
Exposure to hazardous dust — disturbance of deteriorated slab or loose materials during close inspection
Eye injury — dust or debris particles when examining cracks and spalling
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — inspection work at balcony edge above 4m
controls: Complete scaffold handover certificate inspection before any worker accesses platform — confirm guardrails, toe boards, and platform boards are secure and tagged.
Wear fall arrest harness attached to certified anchor point on scaffold frame — harness must be inspected and certified before each shift.
Work only within marked inspection zone on scaffold — stay clear of edge unless harnessed and tethered to fixed anchor.
Dampen slab surface with water spray before close inspection of cracks and spalling — prevent dust generation during defect examination.
Wear dust mask (P2 particulate respirator) when inspecting deteriorated areas or loose materials — fit test must be current.
Wear eye protection— protect against airborne particles.
Photograph defects from stable position on scaffold — never reach over edge or lean beyond guardrail.
Record crack location, size, and condition on defect map in real time — do not rely on memory after leaving scaffold.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not access scaffold platform until: handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and guardrails, toe boards, and platform are verified secure and tagged.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start slab inspection until: engineer confirms inspection scope and permitted access zone on occupied building; working at heights permit is signed and on site.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: fall arrest harness is damaged, anchor point is loose or uncertified, or worker cannot maintain tether to fixed point.
🛑 STOP WORK if: crack pattern or structural damage suggests active movement, settlement, or load-bearing failure — tell engineer immediately before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupied building rules are breached — noise outside agreed hours, tenant safety is compromised, or hazardous debris falls beyond controlled zone.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

Engineer to document all findings, crack mapping, repair scope, and slab condition in writing before approval sign-off.

task_blocks_raw.task: Repair slab cracks and prepare substrate for sealer application
task_blocks_raw.scope: Fill cracks with approved sealant or mortar per engineer instruction. Patch spalling with concrete repair compound. Grind and prepare surface to receipt . Confirm substrate dryness and cleanliness
hazards: Inhalation of dust — grinding or preparation of slab surface generates respirable dust
Chemical exposure — inhalation or skin contact with sealants, repair compounds, or primers
Fall from height — work on scaffold above 4m while carrying tools or repair materials
Musculoskeletal injury — grinding, filling, and surface preparation by hand; repetitive motion and awkward postures
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of dust — grinding and surface preparation of exposed slab
controls: Obtain and read SDS for all sealants, repair compounds, and primers on point of use before application.
Apply wet suppression or dust extraction to all grinding work — no dry grinding of slab surface.
Maintain continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) at grinder discharge point during all surface preparation work.
Confirm substrate is fully dry and clean of dust and debris before applying any sealant or repair compound.
Establish exclusion zone below and around scaffold — no unauthorised entry during repair or grinding work.
Confirm scaffold has valid handover certificate and tag from licenced scaffolder before first use.
Wear respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) during all grinding and surface preparation work.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and face shield when handling or applying sealants, repair compounds, or primers.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply sealant or repair compound until: substrate has been checked dry and confirmed clean of all dust, debris, and contamination by supervisor
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start grinding or surface preparation until: local exhaust ventilation (LEV) is installed, tested, and confirmed operational

🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition is found to contain unknown material, contamination, or differs from engineer scope
🛑 STOP WORK if: building occupants report respiratory distress or dust escape outside exclusion zone

task_blocks_raw.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system to balcony slab
task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply primer to prepared slab. Install new waterproofing membrane per manufacturer specification and engineer detail, including all penetrations, edges, and transitions. Cure per schedule before reinstatement.
hazards: Chemical inhalation or skin exposure — volatile organic compounds or solvents in primer, membrane, or adhesives
Fall from height — applicator movement on scaffold above 4m while carrying membrane rolls or application equipment
Inadequate curing — membrane not cured to specification before foot traffic or weather exposure, causing failure
Heat or UV sensitivity — rapid curing or weather interference affecting membrane bond or integrity
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Chemical inhalation — application of primer and membrane with VOC or solvent content
controls: Obtain and read SDS for primer and membrane product at point of use before any application starts.
Confirm substrate is dry, clean, and free from dust, debris, or contamination — no application if wet or compromised.
Establish continuous forced ventilation across balcony using mechanical extraction or cross-breeze throughout application and cure phases.
Apply primer only when air temperature is 10–25°C and humidity below 85%; stop application if conditions exceed limits.
Install membrane in strict sequence per engineer detail and manufacturer specification — cover all penetrations, edges, and transitions without gaps or overlaps.
Prohibit foot traffic or equipment placement on uncured membrane — establish exclusion zone with barricade and signage.
Maintain cure schedule compliance — do not remove barriers or permit weather exposure until SDS cure time is confirmed elapsed.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection; change gloves immediately if contaminated.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: substrate condition is inspected and signed off by site supervisor and engineer confirms cure window conditions (temperature, humidity, weather forecast) are acceptable for next 48 hours minimum.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove exclusion barrier or allow foot traffic until: cure schedule time has elapsed and SDS cure specification is confirmed complete by applicator or supervisor.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: ventilation fails, wind gusts exceed 15 km/h, or VOC odour becomes strong — cease application until system is restored and air is clear.
🛑 STOP WORK if: temperature drops below 10°C, humidity exceeds 85%, or rain/dew is forecast within cure window — cover and cease work until conditions stabilise.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unexpected substrate condition (cracks, soft spots, contamination, or moisture) is found — obtain engineer approval before proceeding.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

task_blocks_raw.task: Install screed layer and reinstate tiles to balcony surfaces
task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply cement screed bed to cured membrane. Install tiles with appropriate adhesive and grout. Confirm level, slope, and drainage. Make good perimeter jointing.
hazards: Fall from height — installer and tiler movement on scaffold above 4m with tools and materials
Thermal or chemical exposure — screed mixing and cement contact causing skin irritation or chemical burn
Musculoskeletal injury — manual spreading of screed, tile placement, and grouting; repetitive bending and kneeling
Trip or slip on wet screed — newly applied screed before curing, creating slippery surface on scaffold
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — tiler and screed installer on scaffold above 4m
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate and competency tag fitted before any worker accesses scaffold.
Install edge protection (guardrails and toeboard) around all perimeter edges before screed or tiles start.
Wear full-body harness with lanyard clipped to fixed anchor point approved by engineer during all work above 4m.
Place wet screed warning signs on scaffold and adjacent ground areas. Establish no-go exclusion zone until screed cures (minimum 24 hours as per product SDS).
Review SDS for screed and tile adhesive on point of use. Confirm ventilation from occupied spaces below and weather window (no rain forecast, temperature 5–35°C) before starting.
Mix screed in small batches only. Wear chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection, and dust mask (P2) during mixing and application.
Apply screed using trowel or spreader. Do not kneel directly on freshly applied screed; use knee boards or crawling access only.
Set tiles to substrate with notched spreader. Check for void-free bed and level as per product requirements. Do not work on screed until surface has cured per SDS (typically 24 hours minimum).

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install tiles or grout until: screed has cured for minimum 24 hours as confirmed by SDS and product instruction, and PM or licensed screed specialist has checked and signed substrate condition.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection becomes damaged, incomplete, or is removed; harness cannot be clipped to fixed anchor; or worker falls or is near-miss to edge.
🛑 STOP WORK if: rain begins, temperature falls below 5°C or exceeds 35°C, or wind speed exceeds 20 km/h (wind may displace debris netting and equipment).
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed base shows signs of movement, spalling, or unexpected softness; or if adhesive or grout SDS requirements cannot be met (ventilation, cure window, temperature).
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
